topic: Brain has no pain receptors: awake brain surgery, headache origin

slides.title: No pain sensors
slides.body: Brain tissue has no nociceptors, the nerve endings that detect pain.
slides.image_prompt: A glossy anatomical brain model on a dark surface, soft blue rim light, small red warning lights around it all switched off

slides.title: Awake brain surgery
slides.body: So surgeons can operate while patients stay awake and talk.
slides.image_prompt: Empty surgical operating room under bright round surgical lamps, sterile instruments neatly laid on a steel tray, cool clinical tones

slides.title: So why headaches?
slides.body: That pain comes from membranes, blood vessels and nerves around the brain.
slides.image_prompt: Glowing red network of blood vessels and thin nerve fibers wrapped around a translucent brain shape, dark background, medical illustration style

caption:
Your brain processes every pain signal in your body, yet it can't feel pain itself. Brain tissue has no pain receptors, which is why some patients stay awake and talk during brain surgery so surgeons can map speech areas.

The headache you feel comes from the tissue around your brain, not the brain itself. Part 2 tomorrow: where headache pain really starts. Follow so you don't miss it.

Would you agree to stay awake during brain surgery?
